correctness.rationale: PASS: The source Li–Luo–Porter Theorem 5 really establishes a.s. c_e→0 or 1 and convergence of opinions, with c_e→1 implying equal endpoint limiting opinions by contraposition. At each time pre-draw receptive A_e(t) is measurable with respect to the past and the independent next draw selects e with probability 1/|E|. Conditional Borel–Cantelli ensures infinitely many receptive times imply infinitely many SELECTED receptive times almost surely, even if receptive episodes are short. If c_e→0, each such selected event would reset c_e(t+1)>=γ>0, impossible infinitely often. Hence a confidence-zero edge has finitely many receptive times. If c_e→1, opinion gap→0 and confidence→1, so eventually |gap|<c_e permanently. Taking a maximum across finite E proves exactly constant graph a.s. with surviving edges c∞=1. Independent C2_OK rational reset and decay checks verify update algebra but are not a proof of conditional Borel–Cantelli.

evidence: Theorem 5 gives 0/1 confidence limits; Theorem 6 gives cross-cluster eventual exclusion, which is strictly weaker than exact eventual graph constancy.
The general network Borel–Cantelli method supports the sampling lemma but does not specialize to confidence-zero reset contradiction in this model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The source has no broader theorem granting graph stabilization in the adaptive-DW case; its §6.2 explicitly identifies remaining graph behavior as open. The present proof combines established 0/1 limit with an additional predictable-events argument.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified: Li–Luo–Porter (2303.07563v3) explicitly prove only that eventually receptive adaptive-DW edges belong to common opinion-limit clusters, leaving actual eventual graph constancy unproved; this finding fills that particular gap by predictable-time sampling. The newer Thompsky–Wu–Porter–Luo 2605.20418 model adapts selection weights under a fixed radius, not this uniform-selection adaptive-confidence process. Generic stochastic-gossip stopping-time results remain a possible mathematically equivalent source.
residual_risks: An already-known conditional sampling theorem in stochastic gossip may state the same conclusion under other terminology.
The theorem gives no deterministic uniform stabilization time or expected-time estimate.
The fixed selection probability is essential; vanishing adaptive selection weights could invalidate it.
